title: Middle extension on a curve
statement:
Use the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $\Qlb$ is the chosen algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], where dense means that the closure of $j(U_0)$ is all of $C_0$, and $C_0$ is a smooth curve: its structure morphism $C_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $C_0$ has pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension].

For a lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $U_0$ in the finite-extension, adic convention of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] (whose finite-ring lisse convention is [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]), the *sheaf-theoretic middle extension* is $j_*\mathcal F$, where $j_*$ is the ordinary direct image of coefficient sheaves, interpreted in the coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Ordinary module direct image is the sheaf pushforward of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: at a fixed sheaf coefficient stage it has sections
$$
 (j_*G)(V)=G(V\times_{C_0}U_0),
$$
restriction maps induced by base change of $V$, and $(j_*u)_V=u_{V\times_{C_0}U_0}$ on a sheaf morphism $u$; at finite etale coefficient level this is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The coefficient action is the one induced by the coefficient structure map in module direct image.

Thus $(j_*\mathcal F)[1]$ means the ordinary sheaf direct image, placed in degree zero, followed by the cohomological shift [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; at the $\Qlb$ pair-category level the shift is the one of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. The derived direct image is written $Rj_*\mathcal F$ (the right-derived construction at a fixed coefficient stage is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]); its higher cohomology sheaves must be retained in derived adjunction and Verdier-duality formulas.
